choices.text: The price of a call compared with the pot you can win.
Your probability of winning the tournament.
A required bluff on the river.

questions.explanation: You compare the cost of calling with the size of the pot you are calling into.

questions.prompt: Call $20 into a pot that already has $80 in it, and your call closes the action. You are getting…

choices.text: 5 to 1, because you win 100 for a 20 call if the $80 includes only the current pot before your call — recount: risk 20 to win 100.

questions.explanation: If $80 is already there and nobody else can raise, you risk 20 to win 100. That is 5 to 1.

questions.prompt: A call is immediately profitable on raw equity when…

choices.text: Your chance of winning is higher than the break-even percent of the price.
You have position, even with zero equity.

questions.explanation: Break-even percent is call / (pot you win + call). Equity above that is a profitable call if the out is clean and there is no more betting.

choices.text: The equity of a folded hand you already mucked.
The chance you hit a flush.
The extra value from opponents folding when you bet.

questions.explanation: A bet can win immediately when they fold, which a pure check cannot do.
